issues: Scrambled/merged list markers in Article 2: items b and e are run together with adjacent text ("a...; b..." and "ande. empowerment").
Scrambled/merged list markers in Article 5: item f is merged into the preceding text ("and/orf.").
Scrambled/merged list markers in Article 8: item d is merged into the preceding text ("and/ord.").

Minor meaning drift in Article 10: original says violence occurring in the Special Region of Yogyakarta, while the defined 'Region' is Gunungkidul; keep the original meaning but clarify as 'within the Special Region of Yogyakarta' (not 'in the Special Region of Yogyakarta' is acceptable—no change needed beyond faithful rendering).
Scrambled numbering/list markers in Article 12: item (3) appears as '(3)' on its own line and out of the 1–5 sequence; should be '3.' like the other items.
Meaning drift in Article 13(2): refers to 'letter d' but should refer to 'letter a' (the divisions listed in (1) are a–d; 'letter d' is incorrect).
Scrambled/incorrect list reference in Article 13(2): original refers to paragraph (1) letter d, but translation says letter a (meaning drift).
Scrambled/incorrect numbering: Article 24 repeats item "2."; should be (1), (2), (3).

Scrambled list markers: several lettered items are run together (e.g., "andc.", "andi.", "and/ori.") and some paragraph markers (5) and (6) are embedded mid-sentence instead of appearing as separate list items, risking boundary-based retrieval errors.
Meaning drift/awkward rendering: Article 34 translates "terpadu dan terintegrasi" as "integrated and integrated"; should be "integrated and coordinated"/"integrated and interlinked" (distinct terms).
Scrambled/incorrect numbering in Article 24: original has items 1, 2 (with subitems a–c), then 2 again; translation changes the last '2.' to '3.'

Scrambled/formatting of paragraph numbering in Article 25: original has (4), (5), (6) run together; translation keeps (5) and (6) as separate paragraphs but not as list item '5.' and '6.' consistent with the original sequence markers

Scrambled/formatting of paragraph numbering in Article 35: original has (1) and (2) in one run; translation places '(2)' as a separate paragraph but not as list item '2.' consistent with the original sequence markers

Scrambled/merged numbering structure: several paragraph markers are run together on one line (e.g., Article 12 Verse (3) with Verse (4); Article 25 Verse (1)–(7); Article 29 Point b–d), which can break downstream boundary splitting. They should be separated and kept in order.

Minor meaning drift/terminology: 'Ayat' is better rendered as 'Paragraph' (not 'Verse') in legal English; 'PPT' should not be expanded to 'integrated service centers' without basis in the original (keep PPT as in source).
